name: Spinach and Pepper Omelet
description: A four-egg vegetable omelet that keeps you full all morning. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~382 kcal, 28g protein, 8g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 80 g bell pepper (about half a medium pepper) and roughly chop 60 g spinach (2 packed cups).
Crack 200 g eggs (4 large) into a bowl, add a pinch of salt and pepper, and whisk until no streaks of white remain.
Heat 7 g olive oil (1/2 tbsp) in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Sauté the peppers 2-3 minutes until they start to soften.
Add the spinach and cook about 1 minute, until just wilted. Spread the vegetables evenly across the pan.
Pour in the eggs and let them set for 30 seconds, then gently drag the edges toward the center with a spatula, tilting the pan so raw egg fills the gaps.
When the top is just set but still glossy (2-3 minutes), fold the omelet in half, slide onto a plate, and serve immediately.

name: Egg White Veggie Scramble
description: Big volume, tiny calories — egg whites with a whole pan of vegetables. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · Quick · ~224 kcal, 32g protein, 11g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Slice 80 g mushrooms (about 1 cup) and dice 80 g bell pepper (half a medium pepper). Have 50 g spinach (1.5 packed cups) ready.
Heat 5 g olive oil (1 tsp) in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the mushrooms 3-4 minutes until browned and their moisture has cooked off, then add the peppers and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir in the spinach and cook until just wilted, about 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to medium-low and pour in 250 g egg whites (about 1 cup). Let them set for 20-30 seconds, then push gently with a spatula into soft curds.
Cook until the whites are opaque and fluffy with no liquid remaining, 2-3 minutes, and serve right away.

name: Protein Overnight Oats
description: Five minutes tonight, breakfast done tomorrow. High protein · High fiber · ~486 kcal, 38g protein, 66g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Add 60 g rolled oats (2/3 cup) and 30 g whey protein powder (1 scoop) to a jar and stir the dry ingredients together so the whey won't clump.
Pour in 200 g milk (3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp) and stir until everything is evenly wet, scraping the bottom of the jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight, until the oats are soft and the mixture has thickened.
In the morning, stir well; if it's too thick, loosen with a splash of milk or water.
Top with 80 g blueberries (1/2 cup) and eat cold, straight from the jar.

name: Greek Yogurt Berry Bowl
description: Protein-packed yogurt with two kinds of berries. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~242 kcal, 32g protein, 27g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Rinse 70 g blueberries (1/2 cup) and 80 g strawberries (5-6 berries). Hull the strawberries and slice them.
Spoon 300 g nonfat Greek yogurt (1 1/4 cups) into a bowl and smooth the top.
Scatter the blueberries and sliced strawberries over the yogurt.
Serve immediately, or chill covered for up to a day with the berries added just before eating.

name: Cottage Cheese Power Bowl
description: Slow-digesting protein with fruit and crunch. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~347 kcal, 31g protein, 27g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 100 g pineapple (2/3 cup) into bite-size chunks, draining any excess juice.
Spoon 250 g cottage cheese (1 cup) into a bowl.
Top with the pineapple chunks and 15 g almonds (a small handful, about 2 tbsp); roughly chop the almonds first if you prefer smaller pieces.
Season with a small pinch of salt if your cottage cheese is low-sodium, and serve chilled.

name: Turkey Sausage Egg Muffins
description: Bake a batch on Sunday, grab two every morning. High protein · Low carb · ~289 kcal, 28g protein, 4g carbs, 1g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and coat a 12-cup muffin tin generously with cooking spray.
Chop 200 g cooked turkey sausage (about 2 links) into small pieces, dice 120 g bell pepper (1 medium pepper), and finely chop 80 g spinach (2.5 packed cups).
Crack 500 g eggs (10 large) into a large bowl, season with salt and pepper, and whisk until fully blended.
Stir the sausage, peppers, and spinach into the eggs.
Divide the mixture evenly among the muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full; give the bowl a stir between pours so the fillings stay evenly distributed.
Bake 20-22 minutes, until the muffins are puffed and just set in the center (a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean).
Cool 5 minutes in the tin, then run a knife around each muffin to release. Divide into 4 portions of 3 muffins each; refrigerate up to 4 days.

name: Banana Protein Oatmeal
description: Warm oats with whey stirred in and banana on top. High protein · High fiber · ~592 kcal, 41g protein, 86g carbs, 10g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Combine 70 g rolled oats (3/4 cup) and 250 g milk (1 cup) in a small saucepan with a pinch of salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then cook 4-5 minutes, stirring often, until the oats are creamy and most of the milk is absorbed.
Remove the pan from the heat and let it cool for about a minute; stirring whey into liquid that's too hot makes it clump.
Stir in 30 g whey protein powder (1 scoop) until completely smooth, adding a splash of water if the oatmeal gets too thick.
Slice 100 g banana (1 medium) over the top and serve warm.

name: Smoked Salmon Breakfast Plate
description: Eggs, smoked salmon and greens — zero sugar. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~388 kcal, 38g protein, 4g carbs, 1g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Toss 60 g mixed greens (2 cups) with 5 g olive oil (1 tsp), half of the 10 g lemon juice (1 tsp), and a pinch of salt. Arrange on one side of a plate.
Crack 150 g eggs (3 large) into a bowl, season lightly with salt and pepper, and whisk well.
Warm a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat with a little cooking spray. Pour in the eggs.
Stir slowly and constantly with a spatula, pulling the eggs into soft folds; remove from heat while they still look slightly glossy, about 2-3 minutes. They will finish cooking off the heat.
Plate the eggs next to the greens and drape 100 g smoked salmon (4-5 slices) alongside.
Finish the salmon with the remaining lemon juice (1 tsp) and a grind of black pepper.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Toast
description: The classic pre-training breakfast. Weight gain · Quick · ~475 kcal, 20g protein, 62g carbs, 9g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Toast 80 g whole wheat bread (2 slices) until golden and crisp.
While the bread is hot, spread 32 g peanut butter (2 tbsp) evenly across both slices so it softens slightly.
Slice 100 g banana (1 medium) into thin rounds.
Shingle the banana slices over the peanut butter, pressing gently so they stick, and eat immediately while the toast is still warm.

name: Bulk Builder Oatmeal
description: Calorie-dense oats for hard gainers: nut butter, whole milk feel, honey. Weight gain · High fiber · ~923 kcal, 31g protein, 122g carbs, 16g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Combine 90 g rolled oats (1 cup) and 300 g milk (1 1/4 cups) in a saucepan with a pinch of salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Remove from the heat and stir in 30 g almond butter (2 tbsp) and 20 g honey (1 tbsp) until fully melted into the oats.
Transfer to a bowl. Slice 100 g banana (1 medium) over the top.
Finish with 15 g walnuts (2 tbsp), roughly chopped, and serve warm. Add a splash of milk or water if it thickens as it sits.

name: Veggie Egg White Wrap
description: A lean breakfast wrap you can eat one-handed. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~323 kcal, 28g protein, 38g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Thinly slice 60 g bell pepper (half a small pepper).
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat with cooking spray and sauté the peppers 2-3 minutes until softened.
Pour in 200 g egg whites (3/4 cup), season with salt and pepper, and scramble gently until opaque and fluffy with no liquid left, 2-3 minutes.
Warm the 60 g flour tortilla (1 large) in a dry skillet or microwave for 15-20 seconds so it rolls without cracking.
Lay 30 g mixed greens (1 cup) down the center of the tortilla, top with the egg white scramble, and spoon 40 g salsa (2 1/2 tbsp) over the eggs.
Fold in the sides, roll the wrap tightly away from you, and slice in half to serve.

name: Ricotta Berry Breakfast Bowl
description: Creamy ricotta with raspberries — dessert for breakfast. High protein · Vegetarian · ~385 kcal, 32g protein, 32g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Stir 180 g part-skim ricotta (3/4 cup) and 100 g nonfat Greek yogurt (a scant 1/2 cup) together in a bowl until smooth and creamy.
Gently fold in half of the 90 g raspberries (about 1/3 cup), letting them streak the mixture slightly.
Top with the remaining raspberries.
Drizzle 10 g honey (1 1/2 tsp) over the bowl and serve chilled.

name: Blueberry Protein Smoothie
description: Whey, berries and almond milk — 5 minutes, 35 g protein. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~308 kcal, 33g protein, 38g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Add 300 g unsweetened almond milk (1 1/4 cups) to the blender first so the powder doesn't stick to the blades.
Add 40 g whey protein powder (1 1/3 scoops), 120 g blueberries (3/4 cup), and 50 g banana (half a medium banana).
Drop in a small handful of ice cubes.
Blend on high 45-60 seconds, until completely smooth and no berry skins remain.
Pour into a glass and drink immediately; it thickens as it sits.

name: Green Machine Smoothie
description: Spinach you cannot taste, protein you can. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~229 kcal, 24g protein, 29g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Add 250 g unsweetened almond milk (1 cup) and 60 g spinach (2 packed cups) to the blender and blend 20-30 seconds, until the spinach is fully broken down.
Add 120 g pineapple (3/4 cup chunks) and 200 g nonfat Greek yogurt (3/4 cup).
Add a handful of ice, especially if the pineapple is fresh rather than frozen.
Blend on high about 60 seconds, until smooth and pale green with no visible flecks of leaf.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Shake
description: Tastes like a milkshake, works like a meal. High protein · Weight gain · Quick · ~564 kcal, 45g protein, 52g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pour 300 g milk (1 1/4 cups) into the blender.
Add 35 g whey protein powder (1 heaping scoop), 30 g peanut butter (2 tbsp), and 120 g banana (1 large), broken into chunks.
Add a handful of ice cubes.
Blend on high 45-60 seconds, until thick, creamy, and completely smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink right away; a frozen banana makes it even thicker if you plan ahead.

name: Mass Gainer Shake
description: 1,000+ calories you can drink — oats, whey, nut butter and fruit. Weight gain · Quick · ~1002 kcal, 70g protein, 114g carbs, 12g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Add 60 g rolled oats (2/3 cup) to the blender alone and pulse until they grind into a rough flour; this keeps the shake from being gritty.
Pour in 400 g milk (1 2/3 cups) and let the oats sit for a minute to soften.
Add 50 g whey protein powder (about 1 1/2 scoops), 40 g peanut butter (2 1/2 tbsp), 120 g banana (1 large), and 15 g honey (2 tsp).
Blend on high 60-90 seconds, until completely smooth and creamy.
Add a few ice cubes and pulse briefly to chill if desired.
Drink between meals rather than with them so it adds calories instead of replacing food.

name: Strawberry Cheesecake Smoothie
description: Cottage cheese blends into pure creaminess. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~276 kcal, 24g protein, 31g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Hull 150 g strawberries (about 1 cup); frozen berries work too and make a thicker shake.
Add 200 g unsweetened almond milk (3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp) and 200 g cottage cheese (3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp) to the blender.
Add the strawberries and 10 g honey (1 1/2 tsp).
Blend on high 60-90 seconds, until completely silky; cottage cheese needs the extra time to lose its curds.
Taste and blend in a bit more honey if the berries are tart, then pour and serve immediately.

name: Mango Coconut Smoothie
description: A tropical gainer with light coconut milk. Weight gain · Vegetarian · Quick · ~481 kcal, 19g protein, 52g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cube 150 g mango (1 cup chunks) if using fresh; frozen mango works and chills the smoothie.
Pour 150 g light coconut milk (2/3 cup) into the blender.
Add the mango, 80 g banana (1 small), and 150 g nonfat Greek yogurt (2/3 cup).
Add a few ice cubes if all your fruit is fresh rather than frozen.
Blend on high about 60 seconds, until thick, golden, and completely smooth, then pour and serve.

name: Chocolate Recovery Shake
description: Post-workout chocolate whey with a real-food base. High protein · Quick · ~452 kcal, 38g protein, 51g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Chop 15 g dark chocolate (about 2 squares) as finely as you can so it blends smoothly.
Pour 300 g milk (1 1/4 cups) into the blender.
Add 35 g whey protein powder (1 heaping scoop), 100 g banana (1 medium) broken into chunks, and the chopped chocolate.
Add a handful of ice and blend on high 60 seconds, until smooth with only tiny flecks of chocolate remaining.
Drink within 30-60 minutes after training for recovery.

name: Grilled Chicken Power Salad
description: The default cut lunch: half a pound of chicken over greens. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~537 kcal, 71g protein, 11g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 220 g chicken breast (1 large breast) dry and season both sides generously with salt and pepper. If it's thicker than 1 inch, butterfly or pound it even so it cooks uniformly.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 400°F / 200°C) and coat with cooking spray.
Grill the chicken 5-6 minutes per side, until well-marked and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest the chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes while you build the salad.
Halve 100 g cherry tomatoes (2/3 cup) and slice 80 g cucumber (about 1/2 cup) into half-moons.
Whisk 14 g olive oil (1 tbsp) with 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp), a pinch of salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Toss 100 g mixed greens (3-4 cups) with the tomatoes, cucumber, and dressing in a large bowl.
Slice the rested chicken against the grain and lay it over the top. Serve immediately.

name: Chicken Avocado Bowl
description: Chicken, rice and avocado — the balanced default. High protein · ~633 kcal, 62g protein, 53g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 180 g chicken breast (1 medium breast) dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat a grill pan or skillet over medium-high heat with cooking spray and cook the chicken 5-6 minutes per side, until nicely browned and 165°F (74°C) in the center.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice against the grain.
Meanwhile, reheat 180 g cooked brown rice (1 cup) with a splash of water, covered, until steaming.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and season lightly with salt.
Slice 70 g avocado (half a medium avocado) and fan it over the rice, then top with the sliced chicken.
Finish the whole bowl with 10 g lemon juice (2 tsp), a pinch of salt, and black pepper.

name: Tuna Salad Lettuce Wraps
description: Crunchy, cheap, and 40 g of protein. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · Quick · ~343 kcal, 43g protein, 4g carbs, 2g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Drain 160 g canned tuna (one large can) well, pressing out excess water, then flake it into a bowl with a fork.
Dice 50 g celery (1 stalk) into small pieces.
Stir the celery and 20 g olive oil mayo (1 heaping tbsp) into the tuna until evenly coated. Season with salt and pepper.
Separate 80 g mixed greens into whole leaves, keeping the largest, sturdiest leaves for wrapping.
Spoon the tuna salad down the center of each leaf, fold or roll, and eat right away so the leaves stay crisp.

name: Turkey Club Wrap
description: Deli turkey, bacon and greens rolled tight. High protein · Quick · ~473 kcal, 32g protein, 38g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Slice 50 g tomato (half a medium tomato) into thin rounds and pat them dry so the wrap doesn't get soggy.
Crisp 15 g cooked bacon (2 slices) in a dry skillet or microwave for about 30 seconds if it has softened.
Warm 60 g flour tortilla (1 large) in a dry skillet for 15-20 seconds per side until pliable.
Spread 10 g olive oil mayo (2 tsp) over the tortilla, leaving a 1-inch border.
Layer 120 g deli turkey breast (4-5 slices), the bacon, tomato, and 40 g mixed greens (a big handful) down the center. Hit the tomato with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Fold in the ends, roll the wrap tightly away from you, and slice it in half on the diagonal.

name: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
description: Chickpeas, feta and vegetables in a lemon vinaigrette. High fiber · Vegetarian · Weight loss · ~570 kcal, 25g protein, 68g carbs, 17g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Drain and rinse 200 g cooked chickpeas (1 1/4 cups), then pat them dry.
Dice 100 g cucumber (a third of an English cucumber) and 100 g tomato (1 small tomato). Finely dice 30 g onion (1/4 small onion).
In a large bowl, whisk 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) with 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp), a pinch of salt, and black pepper.
Add the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, and onion to the dressing and toss to coat.
Crumble 40 g feta cheese (1/4 cup) over the top and fold it in gently so it doesn't break down.
Let the salad sit 5-10 minutes before eating so the flavors meld.

name: Chicken Burrito Bowl
description: Everything you like about a burrito, none of the tortilla. High protein · High fiber · ~742 kcal, 72g protein, 75g carbs, 17g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 180 g chicken breast (1 medium breast) dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Grill or pan-sear the chicken over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F (74°C) inside.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice it against the grain.
While it rests, warm 150 g cooked brown rice (3/4 cup) and 120 g cooked black beans (3/4 cup, drained) in the microwave or a small pan.
Slice 50 g avocado (about a third of an avocado).
Layer the rice and beans in a bowl, then top with the sliced chicken, 60 g salsa (1/4 cup), and the avocado.

name: Shrimp Zoodle Bowl
description: Garlicky shrimp over zucchini noodles. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~350 kcal, 51g protein, 9g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Spiralize 250 g zucchini (2 medium zucchini) into noodles and pat them dry with paper towels.
Pat 200 g cooked shrimp dry so they sear instead of steam.
Heat 12 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp and toss 1-2 minutes just to heat through — they're already cooked. Remove to a bowl.
Add the zoodles to the hot pan and toss for 2 minutes, until just tender but still with bite. Don't let them go soft and watery.
Return the shrimp, add 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp), season with salt and pepper, toss once, and serve immediately.

name: Lentil Soup with Greens
description: A pot of fiber that eats like a meal. High fiber · Vegetarian · Weight loss · ~360 kcal, 21g protein, 53g carbs, 21g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 80 g onion (1 small onion) and 120 g carrots (2 medium carrots). Strip 100 g kale (3 packed cups) from its stems and chop it.
Heat 14 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a soup pot over medium heat. Sauté the onion and carrots 5-6 minutes until softened.
Stir in 5 g curry powder and spices (2 tsp) and toast 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 400 g cooked lentils (2 cups) and about 3 cups of water. Bring to a simmer and cook 10-15 minutes, until the carrots are tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the kale and simmer 2-3 minutes until wilted and bright green.
Divide into 2 bowls, or cool and portion into 2 containers.

name: Chicken Caesar-ish Salad
description: The Caesar feel from parmesan and mayo — without croutons. High protein · Low carb · ~575 kcal, 72g protein, 5g carbs, 2g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 200 g chicken breast (1 large breast) dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Grill or pan-sear over medium-high heat for 6-7 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F (74°C) inside. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Make the dressing: whisk 20 g olive oil mayo (1 heaping tbsp), 10 g lemon juice (2 tsp), half of the 20 g grated parmesan (about 2 tbsp), and plenty of black pepper. Thin with water, 1 tsp at a time, until it drizzles.
Toss 120 g mixed greens (4 big handfuls) with the dressing until every leaf is coated.
Top with the sliced chicken and the remaining parmesan.

name: Egg Salad Sandwich
description: Old-school egg salad on whole wheat. High protein · Vegetarian · Quick · ~553 kcal, 30g protein, 35g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Place 150 g eggs (3 large eggs) in a pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Cut the heat, cover, and let sit 10-11 minutes.
Move the eggs to ice water for a few minutes, then peel and chop them.
Mix the chopped eggs with 20 g olive oil mayo (1 heaping tbsp), salt, and pepper, mashing lightly so it holds together.
Toast 80 g whole wheat bread (2 slices).
Lay 30 g mixed greens (a handful) on one slice, pile on the egg salad, close the sandwich, and cut in half.

name: Cottage Cheese Veggie Plate
description: A no-cook lunch: cottage cheese with a crunch platter. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · Quick · ~311 kcal, 36g protein, 26g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Rinse the vegetables and pat them dry.
Slice 100 g cucumber (a third of an English cucumber) into thick rounds or spears and cut 100 g bell peppers (1 small pepper) into wide strips.
Halve 100 g cherry tomatoes (2/3 cup) or leave them whole for dipping.
Spoon 300 g cottage cheese (1 1/4 cups) into a bowl set in the middle of a plate and season it with black pepper.
Arrange the vegetables around the bowl and serve chilled, scooping cottage cheese with each bite.

name: Tofu Buddha Bowl
description: Crispy tofu, quinoa and vegetables in soy dressing. Vegetarian · High fiber · ~565 kcal, 35g protein, 53g carbs, 12g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Press 200 g firm tofu (half a block) between paper towels under a weight for 10 minutes, then cut it into 3/4-inch cubes.
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu 8-10 minutes, turning every few minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides.
Meanwhile, warm 150 g cooked quinoa (3/4 cup) and 80 g shelled edamame (1/2 cup).
Shred or julienne 60 g carrots (1 medium carrot) and have 60 g shredded cabbage (3/4 cup) ready.
Build the bowl: quinoa on the bottom, then the tofu, edamame, carrots, and cabbage in sections.
Drizzle 15 g soy sauce (1 tbsp) over everything just before eating.

name: Steak Salad with Avocado
description: Sliced sirloin over greens with avocado. High protein · Low carb · ~561 kcal, 52g protein, 12g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 180 g sirloin steak (a 6 oz steak) dry, season generously with salt and pepper, and let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Grill or sear in a very hot pan for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, 130°F (54°C), or a minute longer per side for medium, 140°F (60°C).
Rest the steak 5 minutes on a cutting board.
While it rests, halve 80 g cherry tomatoes (1/2 cup) and slice 70 g avocado (half an avocado).
Toss 100 g mixed greens (3 big handfuls) with 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) and a pinch of salt.
Slice the steak thinly against the grain and arrange it over the greens with the tomatoes and avocado.

name: Chicken Pesto Wrap
description: Chicken and pesto in a soft tortilla. High protein · ~529 kcal, 53g protein, 33g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 150 g chicken breast (1 small breast) dry and season with salt and pepper.
Pan-sear or grill over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest 5 minutes, then slice thin.
Slice 50 g tomato (half a medium tomato) into thin rounds and pat dry.
Warm 60 g flour tortilla (1 large) in a dry skillet for 15-20 seconds per side until pliable.
Spread 20 g basil pesto (1 heaping tbsp) over the tortilla, then layer the chicken, tomato, and 30 g mixed greens (a handful) down the center.
Fold in the ends, roll tightly, and slice in half.

name: Loaded Baked Potato with Turkey
description: A baked potato that lifts: ground turkey and cheese. High protein · ~680 kcal, 54g protein, 67g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Scrub 300 g russet potato (1 large potato) and prick it all over with a fork.
Bake the potato directly on the rack for 50-60 minutes, until a skewer slides through with no resistance. (Short on time? Microwave 8-10 minutes, flipping halfway.)
While the potato bakes, brown 150 g ground turkey in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, 6-8 minutes until no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Split the hot potato lengthwise, fluff the inside with a fork, and season with a pinch of salt.
Pile on the turkey, then 25 g shredded cheddar (1/4 cup) so it melts from the heat, and finish with 50 g salsa (3 tbsp).

name: Baked Salmon with Asparagus
description: Omega-3s and a sheet pan you barely wash. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~544 kcal, 48g protein, 9g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a sheet pan.
Snap the woody ends off 200 g asparagus (1 bunch) and toss the spears with half of the 10 g olive oil (1 tsp), salt, and pepper.
Pat 200 g salmon fillet dry, rub it with the remaining oil, and season with salt and pepper. Set it on the pan beside the asparagus.
Bake 12-14 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and reaches 145°F (63°C) at the thickest point, and the asparagus is crisp-tender.
Squeeze 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp) over the salmon and asparagus and serve.

name: Garlic Butter Cod with Green Beans
description: Lean white fish that still tastes indulgent. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~403 kcal, 54g protein, 15g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat 220 g cod fillet (1 large fillet) dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Set the cod in a small baking dish and dot the top with 15 g butter (1 tbsp).
Bake 12-15 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily, and reaches 145°F (63°C). Baste once with the melted butter halfway through.
Meanwhile, trim 200 g green beans (2 cups) and steam them 4-5 minutes until crisp-tender.
Stir 10 g lemon juice (2 tsp) into the buttery pan juices, spoon some over the cod, and toss the green beans in the rest.

name: Chicken Stir-Fry
description: Weeknight wok: chicken and five vegetables. High protein · Weight loss · ~546 kcal, 70g protein, 21g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Slice 200 g chicken breast (1 large breast) into thin strips and pat them dry.
Prep the vegetables: cut 120 g broccoli (1 1/2 cups) into small florets, slice 80 g bell peppers (half a large pepper) into strips, cut 60 g carrots (1 medium) into thin coins, and slice 60 g mushrooms (3/4 cup).
Heat 12 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering. Stir-fry the chicken 3-4 minutes until golden and cooked to 165°F (74°C), then remove it.
Add the vegetables and stir-fry 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender, splashing in a tablespoon of water to help the broccoli steam.
Return the chicken, pour in 20 g soy sauce (a generous tbsp), and toss for 1 minute until everything is glazed.

name: Turkey Taco Skillet
description: Taco night in one pan over cauliflower rice. High protein · Low carb · ~441 kcal, 49g protein, 16g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 100 g bell peppers (1 small pepper) into short strips.
Brown 300 g ground turkey in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, 6-8 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in 4 g curry powder and spices (1 1/2 tsp) and the peppers; cook 3-4 minutes until the peppers start to soften.
Add 120 g salsa (1/2 cup) and simmer 2-3 minutes until saucy. Season with salt and pepper.
In a separate pan or the microwave, cook 300 g cauliflower rice (about 3 cups) for 4-5 minutes until tender.
Serve the turkey mixture over the cauliflower rice and top with 40 g shredded cheddar (1/3 cup) so it melts.
Divide into 2 plates or containers.

name: Sirloin with Roasted Brussels
description: Steak night, cut-friendly. High protein · Low carb · ~595 kcal, 66g protein, 18g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Trim and halve 200 g Brussels sprouts (about 2 cups).
Toss the sprouts with 12 g olive oil (1 tbsp), salt, and pepper, spread them cut-side down on a sheet pan, and roast 20-25 minutes until browned with crisp edges.
While they roast, pat 220 g sirloin steak (an 8 oz steak) dry, season generously with salt and pepper, and let it sit at room temperature.
Grill or sear in a very hot pan 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, 130°F (54°C), or 4-5 minutes per side for medium, 140°F (60°C).
Rest the steak 5 minutes, slice against the grain, and serve with the roasted sprouts.

name: Pork Tenderloin with Sweet Potato
description: The leanest red-ish meat there is, plus slow carbs. High protein · ~570 kcal, 59g protein, 52g carbs, 11g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Prick 200 g sweet potato (1 medium) with a fork and put it in to bake — it needs 45-50 minutes total.
Pat 200 g pork tenderloin dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Sear the tenderloin in a hot oven-safe skillet coated with cooking spray, 2-3 minutes per side until browned.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and roast 15-20 minutes, until the pork reaches 145°F (63°C) at the center. Rest 5-10 minutes before slicing.
While the pork rests, steam 150 g green beans (1 1/2 cups) for 4-5 minutes until crisp-tender, then toss with 8 g butter (2 tsp) and a pinch of salt.
Slice the pork into medallions and serve with the split sweet potato and green beans.

name: Shrimp Cauliflower Fried Rice
description: Fried-rice flavor at a third of the calories. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~495 kcal, 63g protein, 17g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 180 g cooked shrimp dry and whisk 100 g eggs (2 large) in a small bowl.
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a large skillet or wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add 300 g cauliflower rice (about 3 cups), spread it flat, and let it sit undisturbed 2 minutes, then stir-fry 3-4 minutes more until the moisture cooks off and it starts to brown.
Push the rice to one side, pour the eggs into the empty side, and scramble until just set, then fold them through the rice.
Add the shrimp and 20 g soy sauce (a generous tbsp) and toss 1-2 minutes, just until the shrimp are heated through. Finish with black pepper.

name: Chicken Parmesan Bake
description: Chicken parm without the breading. High protein · Low carb · ~525 kcal, 77g protein, 10g carbs, 2g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Pat 400 g chicken breasts (2 breasts) dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Sear the chicken in a hot skillet coated with cooking spray, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden — it will finish cooking in the oven.
Arrange the breasts in a baking dish, spoon 200 g marinara sauce (3/4 cup) over them, and top with 80 g part-skim mozzarella (3/4 cup shredded) and 20 g grated parmesan (1/4 cup).
Bake 20-25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots.
Rest 5 minutes, then divide into 2 portions.

name: Beef and Broccoli
description: The takeout classic, cleaned up. High protein · Low carb · ~621 kcal, 61g protein, 18g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 250 g broccoli (about 1 medium head) into bite-size florets and set them next to the stove with a splash of water ready.
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add the ground beef — about 250 g raw 90% lean to yield 200 g cooked — and break it up with a spatula. Cook 6-8 minutes until browned with no pink remaining, then push it to one side of the pan.
Add the broccoli florets with 2 tablespoons of water, cover, and steam 3-4 minutes until bright green and crisp-tender.
Uncover, pour in 25 g soy sauce (1 1/2 tbsp), and toss everything together for 1 minute so the sauce coats the beef and glazes the broccoli.
Season with black pepper to taste and serve hot straight from the skillet.

name: Baked Tilapia with Rice Pilaf
description: Mild fish, lemon, and fluffy rice. High protein · ~636 kcal, 65g protein, 62g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a sheet pan with foil or parchment.
Pat 220 g tilapia fillets (2 small fillets) dry with paper towels, rub with 8 g olive oil (2 tsp), and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Trim 150 g green beans and spread them on the pan beside the fish; hit them with cooking spray and a pinch of salt.
Drizzle 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp) over the fillets and bake 12-14 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork and reaches 145°F (63°C) inside.
While the fish bakes, reheat 180 g cooked white rice (1 cup) in the microwave with a sprinkle of water, covered, about 90 seconds until steaming.
Fluff the rice onto a plate, lay the tilapia on top, add the green beans alongside, and spoon any lemony pan juices over the fish.

name: Turkey Meatballs in Marinara
description: Meal-prep hero — freeze half the batch. High protein · ~551 kcal, 63g protein, 13g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a sheet pan with parchment.
In a large bowl, combine the ground turkey — about 500 g raw 93% lean to yield 400 g cooked — with 50 g egg (1 large) and 30 g grated parmesan (1/3 cup). Season with salt and pepper and mix gently just until combined; overmixing makes tough meatballs.
With damp hands, roll the mixture into 12 even meatballs (about golf-ball size) and space them out on the pan.
Bake 18 minutes, until browned outside and 165°F (74°C) at the center.
Meanwhile, warm 300 g marinara sauce (1 1/4 cups) in a wide saucepan over medium-low heat.
Transfer the baked meatballs into the sauce and simmer gently 5 minutes so they soak up the marinara.
Divide into 2 portions — 6 meatballs with sauce each — and serve or pack into containers.

name: Salmon Rice Bowl
description: The gym-rat special: salmon, rice, avocado. High protein · Weight gain · ~818 kcal, 53g protein, 68g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat 200 g salmon fillet (1 large fillet) dry and season with salt and pepper.
Place the salmon skin-side down on a foil-lined pan and bake 10-12 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 125-130°F (52-54°C) for moist, just-cooked fish.
While the salmon bakes, reheat 220 g cooked white rice (1 1/4 cups) covered in the microwave with a splash of water, about 90 seconds until steaming, and spoon it into a bowl.
Slice 70 g avocado (1/2 medium) into thin fans.
Flake the hot salmon into large chunks over the rice, discarding the skin if you like, and arrange the avocado alongside.
Drizzle 15 g soy sauce (1 tbsp) over the whole bowl and eat while warm.

name: Lemon Herb Roast Chicken Thighs
description: Crispy thighs with roasted carrots. High protein · Low carb · ~524 kcal, 53g protein, 13g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Peel 250 g carrots (3 medium) and cut them into thick diagonal coins; toss them on a sheet pan with half of the 12 g olive oil (use about 1/2 tbsp) and a pinch of salt.
Pat the chicken thighs dry — about 550 g raw bone-in thighs (4 thighs) to yield 400 g roasted meat — then rub with the remaining oil and season generously with salt, pepper, and any dried herbs you have on hand.
Nestle the thighs skin-side up among the carrots and roast 35 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the thickest thigh reads 175°F (79°C) at the bone.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes on the pan so the juices settle.
Squeeze 20 g lemon juice (1 1/2 tbsp) over the chicken and carrots, scrape up the pan juices, and divide into 2 portions of 2 thighs with half the carrots each.

name: Zucchini Lasagna
description: Lasagna layers with zucchini standing in for pasta. High protein · Low carb · Vegetarian · ~432 kcal, 34g protein, 24g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Slice 400 g zucchini (2 medium) lengthwise into 1/4-inch planks.
Salt the planks lightly, let them sit 10 minutes on paper towels, then pat dry — this keeps the lasagna from going watery.
In a bowl, stir together 250 g part-skim ricotta (1 cup) and 50 g egg (1 large) with a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth.
In a baking dish, spread a thin layer of the 250 g marinara, then layer zucchini planks, half the ricotta mixture, and more sauce; repeat with the remaining zucchini, ricotta, and sauce.
Scatter 100 g shredded part-skim mozzarella (1 cup) over the top.
Bake uncovered 35 minutes, until the cheese is browned in spots and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes so it slices cleanly.
Cut into 2 portions and serve, or cool and pack into 2 containers.

name: Stuffed Bell Peppers
description: Peppers packed with beef, rice and tomato. High protein · ~567 kcal, 48g protein, 33g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Halve 300 g bell peppers (2 large) through the stem and pull out the seeds and ribs. Arrange them cut-side up in a baking dish with a splash of water in the bottom.
In a skillet over medium heat, warm the ground beef — about 375 g raw 90% lean to yield 300 g cooked — breaking it up until browned with no pink, 6-8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir 150 g cooked brown rice (3/4 cup) and 120 g marinara sauce (1/2 cup) into the beef and heat through, about 2 minutes.
Pack the filling into the pepper halves, mounding it slightly, and top with 40 g shredded cheddar (1/3 cup).
Bake 25 minutes, until the peppers are tender when pierced and the cheese is melted and browning at the edges.
Divide into 2 portions of 2 pepper halves each.

name: Chicken Curry with Cauliflower
description: A weeknight curry in light coconut milk. High protein · Low carb · ~553 kcal, 60g protein, 17g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 80 g onion (1 small) and cut 300 g cauliflower (1/2 medium head) into small florets.
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 3-4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add 8 g curry powder and spices (1 tbsp) and stir 30 seconds until fragrant — toasting the spices in the oil wakes them up.
Add the cauliflower and 200 g light coconut milk (3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp) with a splash of water and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, grill or pan-sear the chicken — about 440 g raw breast to yield 350 g cooked — over medium-high heat 5-6 minutes per side until 165°F (74°C) inside, then cut into bite-size chunks.
Stir the chicken into the curry and simmer uncovered 5-7 more minutes, until the cauliflower is tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Taste, adjust salt, and divide into 2 bowls or containers.

name: Big Bulk Pasta with Beef
description: The classic gainer dinner: a mountain of pasta and beef marinara. High protein · Weight gain · ~892 kcal, 61g protein, 88g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta — about 200 g dry to yield 500 g cooked — per package directions until al dente. Reserve a splash of pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the ground beef — about 375 g raw 90% lean to yield 300 g cooked — and brown it 6-8 minutes, breaking it into crumbles, until no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour in 250 g marinara sauce (1 cup) and simmer 5 minutes so the flavors merge.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet with a splash of the reserved pasta water and toss until every piece is coated and glossy.
Divide into 2 big portions and shower each with half of the 30 g grated parmesan (1/3 cup total).

name: Chicken Alfredo-ish Pasta
description: A lighter creamy pasta built on ricotta. High protein · Weight gain · ~700 kcal, 71g protein, 57g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Grill or pan-sear the chicken — about 375 g raw breast to yield 300 g cooked — over medium-high heat 5-6 minutes per side until 165°F (74°C) inside. Rest 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the whole wheat pasta — about 160 g dry to yield 400 g cooked — until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of the starchy pasta water before draining.
For the sauce, blend 150 g part-skim ricotta (2/3 cup), 30 g grated parmesan (1/3 cup), and about 1/2 cup of the hot pasta water until completely smooth — a blender or vigorous whisking both work.
Return the drained pasta to the warm pot over low heat with 10 g butter (2 tsp) and toss to coat.
Pour in the ricotta sauce and toss 1-2 minutes, adding more pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is silky and clings to the noodles. Do not boil or the ricotta can turn grainy.
Fold in the sliced chicken, season with salt and plenty of black pepper, and divide into 2 portions.

name: Loaded Sweet Potato and Beef Skillet
description: One skillet: beef, sweet potato cubes, greens. High protein · High fiber · ~713 kcal, 58g protein, 45g carbs, 10g fiber per serving.
instructions:
If starting fresh, bake a 250 g sweet potato at 400°F (200°C) for 45-50 minutes until a knife slides in easily — you need 200 g baked (1 medium). Cube it, skin on or off.
Strip 80 g kale (2 big handfuls) from its stems and tear into bite-size pieces.
Heat 8 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the ground beef — about 250 g raw 90% lean to yield 200 g cooked — and brown 6-8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the cubed sweet potato and let it sit undisturbed 2 minutes to pick up some browning, then toss with the beef.
Pile in the kale with a tablespoon of water and toss 2-3 minutes until wilted and bright green. Serve hot from the skillet.

name: Tofu Veggie Stir-Fry
description: Plant-based and still 30 g of protein. Vegetarian · High fiber · Weight loss · ~475 kcal, 36g protein, 28g carbs, 11g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Press 250 g firm tofu (2/3 block) between paper towels under a heavy plate for 10 minutes, then cut into 1-inch cubes. Dry tofu crisps; wet tofu steams.
Cut 150 g broccoli into small florets and slice 80 g bell peppers (1/2 large pepper) into strips.
Heat 12 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a wok or large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook undisturbed 3 minutes, then turn and crisp the other sides, 5-6 minutes total, until golden. Remove to a plate.
Add the broccoli and peppers to the hot pan with 2 tablespoons of water; stir-fry 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Toss in 80 g shelled edamame (1/2 cup) and cook 1 minute to heat through.
Return the tofu, pour 20 g soy sauce (1 1/4 tbsp) around the edge of the pan, and toss everything 1 minute until glazed. Serve immediately.

name: Protein Yogurt Cup
description: Yogurt with a scoop of whey folded in — pudding, basically. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~193 kcal, 35g protein, 10g carbs, 0g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Spoon 200 g nonfat Greek yogurt (3/4 cup) into a bowl or jar.
Add 20 g whey protein powder (2 heaping tbsp, about 2/3 scoop) on top.
Stir slowly at first so the powder doesn't puff out, then mix vigorously 30-60 seconds until completely smooth with no dry pockets.
If it thickens too much, loosen with a teaspoon of water at a time to your preferred texture. Eat right away or chill covered up to 2 days.

name: Apple with Peanut Butter
description: The snack that never gets old. Quick · Vegetarian · ~241 kcal, 7g protein, 30g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Wash 180 g apple (1 medium) and pat it dry.
Cut the apple into 8 wedges around the core, or slice into thin rounds and punch out the seeds.
Spoon 25 g peanut butter (1 1/2 tbsp) into a small dish; a 10-second microwave zap makes it extra dippable.
Dip the slices as you go. If packing ahead, toss the slices with a little lemon juice or cold water to slow browning and pack the peanut butter separately.

name: Hard-Boiled Egg Pack
description: Three eggs, ready when you are. High protein · Low carb · Quick · ~214 kcal, 19g protein, 1g carbs, 0g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Place 150 g eggs (3 large) in a saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch.
Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, then cut the heat, cover, and let the eggs sit 9-10 minutes for firm, fully set yolks.
Meanwhile fill a bowl with ice water. Transfer the eggs straight into it and chill 5 minutes — the shock stops the cooking and makes peeling easier.
Tap each egg all over, peel starting from the fat end where the air pocket is, and rinse off any shell bits.
Eat with a pinch of salt and pepper, or store peeled in the fridge up to 4 days.

name: Cottage Cheese with Berries
description: Casein-slow protein for the evening. High protein · Weight loss · Quick · ~210 kcal, 23g protein, 18g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Spoon 200 g 2% cottage cheese (3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp) into a bowl or jar.
Give it a quick stir to loosen the curds; add a tiny pinch of salt if your brand runs bland.
Rinse 80 g raspberries (2/3 cup) gently under cold water and let them drain — pat softly, they bruise easily.
Pile the raspberries on top, lightly crushing a few with a fork so their juice streaks the cottage cheese, and eat right away or lid it for a grab-and-go snack.

name: Turkey Roll-Ups
description: Deli turkey wrapped around cheese — zero prep. High protein · Low carb · Quick · ~218 kcal, 27g protein, 8g carbs, 0g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 40 g part-skim mozzarella into sticks roughly the length of your deli slices.
Lay out 100 g deli turkey breast (4-5 slices) flat on a cutting board and grind a little black pepper over them.
Place a stick of mozzarella at the edge of each slice and roll the turkey up snugly around it; slice each roll in half on the diagonal if you like.
Cut 80 g cucumber (1/3 medium) into spears and sprinkle with a pinch of salt.
Arrange the roll-ups and cucumber spears on a plate, or pack them in a container with a paper towel to catch moisture. Keeps refrigerated 2 days.

name: Hummus Veggie Plate
description: Fiber-forward dipping. High fiber · Vegetarian · Quick · ~232 kcal, 10g protein, 30g carbs, 10g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Slice 80 g bell peppers (1/2 large pepper) into strips, discarding the seeds and ribs.
Peel 80 g carrots (1 large) and cut into sticks about the length of your finger.
Cut 80 g cucumber (1/3 medium) into spears; pat them dry so they don't water down the hummus.
Spoon 100 g hummus (a scant 1/2 cup) into a small bowl and swirl the top with the back of the spoon.
Arrange the vegetables around the hummus and serve, or pack the hummus in a lidded cup with the veggies alongside for a portable snack.

name: Rice Cakes with Almond Butter
description: Pre-workout carbs with staying power. Quick · Vegetarian · ~305 kcal, 8g protein, 40g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Lay out 27 g rice cakes (3 standard cakes) on a plate.
Stir the almond butter in its jar if the oil has separated, then spread 24 g (1 1/2 tbsp) evenly across the three cakes.
Peel and slice 60 g banana (1/2 medium) into thin coins.
Shingle the banana slices over the almond butter, pressing lightly so they stick, and finish with a tiny pinch of salt if you like. Eat soon after assembling — rice cakes soften as they sit.

name: Trail Fuel Mix
description: Nuts, dark chocolate and no filler. Weight gain · Quick · Vegetarian · ~414 kcal, 10g protein, 22g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Chop 20 g dark chocolate 70% (2 large squares) into small chip-size chunks with a sharp knife.
Measure 30 g almonds (about 23 nuts) and 20 g walnuts (7-8 halves), breaking any huge walnut pieces in half.
Toss the nuts and chocolate together in a bowl or zip-top bag until evenly mixed.
Eat as one snack portion, and store any batch you scale up in an airtight container away from heat so the chocolate doesn't melt.

name: Tuna Cucumber Bites
description: Tuna salad on cucumber rounds. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · Quick · ~259 kcal, 32g protein, 4g carbs, 1g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Drain 120 g canned tuna (1 can) well, pressing out the water with the lid or a fork.
In a small bowl, mix the tuna with 15 g olive oil mayo (1 tbsp) until evenly coated, then season with salt and pepper.
Slice 120 g cucumber (about half a large cucumber) into thick rounds, roughly 1/2 inch each, and pat the tops dry so the tuna stays put.
Spoon a mound of tuna salad onto each cucumber round and finish with a crack of black pepper. Eat right away or chill up to a day.

name: Cheese and Apple Plate
description: Sweet, sharp, done. Quick · Vegetarian · ~239 kcal, 10g protein, 21g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Core 150 g apple (1 medium) and cut it into thin wedges.
Slice 40 g cheddar cheese (about 4 thin slices) into pieces roughly the size of the apple wedges.
Arrange both on a plate and eat them together, a slice of cheddar with each apple wedge. If prepping ahead, toss the apple wedges with a little lemon juice or cold water to slow browning.

name: Edamame with Sea Salt
description: Steam-and-salt plant protein. Vegetarian · High fiber · Quick · ~182 kcal, 18g protein, 13g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Bring about an inch of water to a boil in a pot fitted with a steamer basket, or set a covered microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp water.
Steam 150 g shelled edamame (1 cup) for 5 minutes, or microwave covered for 2-3 minutes, until the beans are bright green and tender.
Drain well, then toss in a bowl with a generous pinch of flaky sea salt while still hot so the salt sticks.
Serve warm, or chill and eat cold as a snack.

name: Chocolate Yogurt Bark
description: Freeze yogurt with chocolate for a cut-friendly dessert. Weight loss · Vegetarian · ~133 kcal, 11g protein, 15g carbs, 1g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Stir 400 g nonfat Greek yogurt (1 2/3 cups) with 15 g honey (2 tsp) until smooth, then spread it over the parchment in an even layer about 1/4 inch thick.
Hull and slice 100 g strawberries (about 7 berries) and roughly chop 40 g dark chocolate 70% (4 squares).
Scatter the strawberries and chocolate over the yogurt, pressing them in lightly so they set into the surface.
Freeze flat for at least 3 hours, until completely firm.
Break the sheet into shards and divide into 4 portions. Store in the freezer and eat straight from frozen; it softens fast at room temperature.

name: Chickpea Curry
description: Pantry curry that happens to be vegan. Vegetarian · High fiber · Weight loss · ~569 kcal, 21g protein, 67g carbs, 18g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 80 g onion (1/2 medium) and 150 g tomato (1 medium).
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in 8 g curry powder and spices (1 tbsp) and toast for 30-60 seconds, until fragrant; don't let it burn.
Add the tomato and cook 2-3 minutes until it breaks down into a rough paste.
Add 400 g cooked chickpeas (2 1/3 cups, drained) and 200 g light coconut milk (3/4 cup plus a splash). Bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens enough to coat the chickpeas. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Season with salt to taste and divide into 2 bowls or containers.

name: Black Bean Quesadillas
description: Crispy flour tortilla, beans and melted cheddar. Vegetarian · High fiber · ~601 kcal, 31g protein, 69g carbs, 16g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Warm 150 g cooked black beans (3/4 cup, drained) briefly, then mash them in a bowl with 50 g salsa (3 tbsp) until mostly smooth with some whole beans left. Season with salt and pepper.
Lay a 60 g flour tortilla (1 large) flat and spread the bean mixture over one half, leaving a small border.
Scatter 50 g shredded cheddar cheese (1/2 cup) over the beans and fold the tortilla into a half-moon, pressing down gently.
Heat a dry nonstick skillet over medium heat. Toast the quesadilla 2-3 minutes per side, pressing with a spatula, until both sides are golden and crisp and the cheese is fully melted.
Rest 1 minute, then cut into wedges and serve.

name: Caprese Pasta
description: Tomato, mozzarella and pesto through warm pasta. Vegetarian · ~502 kcal, 27g protein, 60g carbs, 9g fiber per serving.
instructions:
If starting from dry pasta, boil enough whole wheat pasta in salted water to yield 400 g cooked (about 3 cups); reserve a splash of the cooking water and drain.
While the pasta cooks, halve 200 g cherry tomatoes (1 1/4 cups) and cut 120 g part-skim mozzarella (1 cup) into small cubes.
Return the hot drained pasta to the pot off the heat. Add 40 g basil pesto (2 heaping tbsp) and toss until every piece is coated, loosening with a spoonful of the reserved pasta water if needed.
Fold in the cherry tomatoes and mozzarella off the heat so the cheese softens at the edges without fully melting.
Season with salt and pepper, then divide between 2 bowls or containers. Good warm or cold.

name: Lentil Bolognese
description: Lentils do the beef's job in this ragù. Vegetarian · High fiber · Weight loss · ~495 kcal, 24g protein, 87g carbs, 22g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 60 g onion (1/2 small) and 80 g carrots (1 medium) finely.
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot with a pinch of salt for 6-8 minutes, until soft and starting to brown.
Add 300 g cooked lentils (1 1/2 cups, drained) and 250 g marinara sauce (1 cup). Stir in a splash of water to loosen.
Simmer 10-12 minutes over low heat, stirring occasionally, until thick and saucy. Mash some of the lentils against the pan for a meatier texture. Season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, warm 300 g cooked whole wheat pasta (2 1/4 cups), or boil dry pasta to yield that amount.
Spoon the lentil sauce over the pasta and divide into 2 portions.

name: Egg Fried Quinoa
description: Fried-rice technique, quinoa base. Vegetarian · High protein · ~636 kcal, 34g protein, 62g carbs, 11g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Crack 100 g eggs (2 large) into a bowl, beat with a pinch of salt, and set aside. Have 250 g cooked quinoa (1 1/3 cups) ready; cold, day-old quinoa fries best.
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a large skillet or wok over high heat until shimmering.
Add the quinoa and 80 g shelled edamame (1/2 cup). Spread flat and let sit 1-2 minutes to crisp, then stir-fry another 2 minutes.
Push everything to one side of the pan. Pour the eggs into the empty side and scramble, stirring, until just set, about 1 minute.
Fold the eggs into the quinoa, add 15 g soy sauce (1 tbsp), and toss over high heat for 1 more minute so everything is coated and hot.
Season with pepper and serve immediately.

name: Halloumi-Style Feta Sheet Pan
description: Roasted vegetables with warm feta. Vegetarian · Low carb · ~476 kcal, 18g protein, 23g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Cut 150 g zucchini (1 medium) into thick half-moons, 150 g bell peppers (1 large) into chunks, and 60 g onion (1/2 small) into wedges.
Toss the vegetables on the pan with 14 g olive oil (1 tbsp), salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are starting to soften and brown at the edges.
Pull the pan out, stir the vegetables, and nestle the 100 g feta cheese block (kept whole) in the center.
Return to the oven for 8 more minutes, until the feta is soft and golden on top and the vegetables are charred at the edges.
Break the feta over the vegetables and serve straight from the pan.

name: Tofu Scramble
description: The vegan scramble that converts skeptics. Vegetarian · Low carb · Weight loss · Quick · ~316 kcal, 23g protein, 12g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Press 250 g firm tofu (about 2/3 block) between paper towels for a few minutes to remove excess water, then crumble it into bite-size pieces with your hands.
Dice 80 g tomato (1/2 large) and rinse 60 g spinach (2 big handfuls).
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the crumbled tofu and 3 g curry powder and spices (1 tsp) with a good pinch of salt.
Cook 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tofu is evenly yellow-tinted and starting to brown in spots.
Add the tomato and spinach and cook 3-4 more minutes, until the spinach wilts and the tomato softens.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

name: Bean and Cheese Stuffed Sweet Potato
description: A whole meal inside a potato skin. Vegetarian · High fiber · ~562 kcal, 27g protein, 91g carbs, 22g fiber per serving.
instructions:
If the sweet potato isn't already baked, prick a 250 g sweet potato (1 medium-large) all over with a fork and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 45-55 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance; or microwave 6-8 minutes, turning halfway.
Warm 150 g cooked black beans (3/4 cup, drained) in a small pan or the microwave, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Split the hot sweet potato lengthwise and fluff the flesh with a fork, pushing the sides apart to make a well.
Pile in the warm beans and top with 30 g shredded cheddar cheese (1/3 cup) so it melts from the heat.
Spoon 50 g salsa (3 tbsp) over the top and serve.

name: Garlic Roasted Broccoli
description: The side that makes fiber automatic. Vegetarian · High fiber · Low carb · Quick · ~134 kcal, 6g protein, 13g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Cut 400 g broccoli (1 large head) into even, medium florets and pat them completely dry; wet broccoli steams instead of browning.
Toss the florets on a sheet pan with 15 g olive oil (1 tbsp), a generous pinch of salt, pepper, and minced garlic or garlic powder to taste. Spread in a single layer, cut sides down.
Roast for 20 minutes without stirring, until the stems are tender and the edges are deeply browned and lightly charred.
Taste for salt and divide into 2 portions.

name: Herbed Cauliflower Mash
description: Mashed-potato comfort at a fraction of the carbs. Vegetarian · Low carb · Weight loss · ~147 kcal, 6g protein, 14g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 500 g cauliflower (1 medium head) into small, even florets.
Steam the florets over boiling water for 10-12 minutes, until completely tender; a fork should meet no resistance. Drain and let sit 2 minutes so excess steam escapes.
Transfer the hot cauliflower to a blender or food processor with 20 g butter (1 1/2 tbsp) and 50 g 2% milk (3 tbsp).
Blend until completely smooth and whipped, scraping down the sides; add another splash of milk only if needed to get it moving.
Season well with salt, pepper, and any dried or fresh herbs you like. Divide into 2 portions and serve hot.

name: Meal-Prep Chicken Breast
description: A kilo of chicken for the week's bowls and salads. High protein · Low carb · ~457 kcal, 78g protein, 0g carbs, 0g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 1000 g chicken breast (4 large breasts) dry with paper towels. Halve any very thick breasts horizontally or pound to an even thickness so they cook uniformly.
Rub all over with 20 g olive oil (1 1/2 tbsp), then season generously on both sides with salt and pepper.
To grill or pan-sear: cook over medium-high heat 5-7 minutes per side, without moving, until deeply browned and the internal temperature reads 165°F (74°C) at the thickest point.
To bake instead: arrange on a sheet pan and roast at 400°F (200°C) for 20-25 minutes to the same 165°F (74°C) internal temperature.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes before slicing so the juices stay in the meat.
Slice against the grain, divide into 4 containers, and refrigerate up to 4 days.

name: Meal-Prep Rice and Beans
description: The cheap, high-fiber carb base for four bowls. Vegetarian · High fiber · ~350 kcal, 13g protein, 62g carbs, 11g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Have 600 g cooked brown rice (about 3 cups) ready; if cooking fresh, simmer dry brown rice in salted water per package timing, then drain and fluff.
Drain and rinse 400 g cooked black beans (2 1/3 cups, about 1 1/2 cans).
Warm 15 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a large skillet over medium heat, add the beans, and heat 2-3 minutes, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Fold the rice into the beans and stir until everything is hot and evenly mixed, about 2 minutes.
Cool briefly, then divide evenly into 4 containers. Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat with a splash of water to loosen.

name: Roasted Sweet Potato Cubes
description: Sweet, slow carbs for any plate. Vegetarian · High fiber · ~233 kcal, 4g protein, 41g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Scrub 600 g sweet potato (2 large) and cut into even 3/4-inch cubes; no need to peel.
Toss the cubes on a sheet pan with 18 g olive oil (4 tsp), salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer with space between the pieces so they roast rather than steam.
Roast for 25 minutes, flipping once halfway, until the cubes are browned and caramelized at the edges and tender in the center.
Cool slightly, then divide into 3 portions. They reheat well in a hot skillet or oven to re-crisp.

name: Sautéed Garlic Green Beans
description: Crisp-tender beans in browned butter. Vegetarian · Low carb · Quick · ~127 kcal, 4g protein, 14g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Wash 400 g green beans (about 4 cups) and trim off the stem ends. Pat them very dry so they blister instead of steaming.
Heat a large skillet over high heat until hot, then add 18 g butter (1 1/4 tbsp) and swirl until it foams.
Add the green beans in as close to a single layer as you can. Let them sit undisturbed for 1-2 minutes to blister, then toss.
Cook 4-5 more minutes total, tossing occasionally, adding minced garlic in the last minute so it turns golden without burning.
Season with salt and pepper; the beans are done when they're blistered and browned in spots but still crisp-tender. Divide into 2 portions.

name: Zucchini Ribbon Salad
description: Raw zucchini, lemon, parmesan. Vegetarian · Low carb · Weight loss · Quick · ~123 kcal, 6g protein, 6g carbs, 2g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Trim 300 g zucchini (2 medium) and shave lengthwise into thin ribbons with a vegetable peeler, rotating as you go and stopping at the seedy core.
In a large bowl, whisk 12 g olive oil (2 1/2 tsp) with 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp), a pinch of salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Add the zucchini ribbons and toss gently with your hands until every ribbon is coated.
Let sit 5 minutes so the ribbons soften slightly and release a little liquid, then toss once more.
Shave 20 g parmesan cheese (1/4 cup) over the top with the peeler, finish with pepper, and divide into 2 portions. Best eaten within a few hours.

name: Cabbage Crunch Slaw
description: The crunchy side that keeps for days. Vegetarian · High fiber · Weight loss · ~162 kcal, 3g protein, 14g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Shred 300 g cabbage (about 4 cups) finely if not pre-shredded, and grate 100 g carrots (1 1/2 medium) on the large holes of a box grater.
In a large bowl, whisk 30 g olive oil mayo (2 tbsp) with 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp), a pinch of salt, and black pepper until smooth to make the dressing.
Add the cabbage and carrots to the bowl and toss thoroughly until the dressing coats every shred.
Chill for at least 10 minutes so the flavors meld and the cabbage softens slightly while keeping its crunch.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon, then divide into 2 portions. Keeps 2 days refrigerated.

name: The Comeback Omelet
description: Chris's lifting-day opener: 4 eggs, spinach, peppers, turkey sausage. No corn, no seeds. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~577 kcal, 45g protein, 19g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Crack 200 g eggs (4 large) into a bowl and whisk with a pinch of salt and pepper until uniform.
Dice 60 g bell pepper (about half a pepper) and slice 80 g cooked turkey sausage into coins.
Heat 7 g olive oil (1/2 tbsp) in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and saute the pepper 2-3 minutes until it softens.
Add 50 g spinach (2 big handfuls) and the sausage; cook about 1 minute until the spinach wilts and the sausage is warmed through.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables, drop the heat to medium-low, and cook undisturbed about 2 minutes until the edges set, lifting the edges to let raw egg run underneath.
When the top is just set but still glossy, fold the omelet in half and slide it onto a plate.
Serve with 80 g blueberries (1/2 cup) on the side.

name: Comeback Chicken Salad Bowl
description: The big lunch: half a pound of chicken, olive-oil vinaigrette, avocado. Seed-free by design. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~655 kcal, 75g protein, 15g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 230 g chicken breast (1 large breast) dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Grill or pan-sear over medium-high heat 5-6 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C); rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk 15 g olive oil (1 tbsp) and 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp) with a pinch of salt and pepper to make the dressing.
Halve 80 g cherry tomatoes (1/2 cup) and slice 80 g cucumber (about half a cucumber) into half-moons.
Toss 100 g mixed greens (about 4 cups) with the tomatoes, cucumber, and dressing in a large bowl.
Top with the sliced chicken and 60 g avocado (1/3 avocado), sliced.

name: Comeback Salmon Plate
description: The lifting-day closer: salmon, roasted potatoes, asparagus — done 3 hours before bed. High protein · Weight loss · ~900 kcal, 70g protein, 52g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut 220 g potato (1 medium) into wedges and toss with half of the 10 g olive oil (use about 1 tsp) and salt.
Spread the potatoes on a sheet pan and roast 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, snap the woody ends off 150 g asparagus, pat 280 g salmon fillet dry, and rub both with the remaining oil, salt, and pepper.
Pull the pan out, push the potatoes to one side, and add the salmon skin-side down with the asparagus alongside.
Roast another 12-13 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 145°F (63°C) and the potatoes are browned and tender.
Plate the salmon with the potato wedges and asparagus; finish with a crack of pepper.

name: Fast-Window Beef Bowl
description: Tue/Thu 12:30 meal: beef over cauliflower rice with cheese and guacamole-style avocado. High protein · Low carb · ~921 kcal, 87g protein, 22g carbs, 11g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the lean ground beef (280 g cooked weight — start with about 350 g raw), breaking it up with a spatula.
Season with salt and pepper and cook 7-8 minutes until no pink remains; drain if needed.
In a second pan (or the same one, beef set aside), saute 250 g cauliflower rice (about 2 1/2 cups) over medium-high 4-5 minutes until tender; season with salt.
Spoon the cauliflower rice into a bowl and pile the hot beef on top.
Scatter 30 g cheddar (1/4 cup shredded) over the beef so it melts.
Finish with 70 g avocado (about half an avocado), diced, and 50 g salsa (3 tbsp).

name: Break-Fast Eggs and Salmon
description: The 9am fast-breaker: eggs, smoked salmon, sautéed greens. High protein · Low carb · ~504 kcal, 47g protein, 4g carbs, 2g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Whisk 200 g eggs (4 large) with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat 8 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a nonstick skillet over medium heat and wilt 80 g spinach (3 big handfuls) 1-2 minutes; slide it onto your plate.
Lower the heat, pour in the eggs, and scramble slowly, stirring often, until they form soft curds that are just set.
Plate the eggs next to the spinach, drape 110 g smoked salmon alongside, and finish with black pepper.

name: Final-Meal Chicken Thighs
description: The 3:15pm fast-window closer: thighs, big salad, yogurt and berries to stretch the fast. High protein · Low carb · ~780 kcal, 80g protein, 21g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Pat 230 g chicken thighs (about 2 thighs) dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Roast on a sheet pan 25-30 minutes until the skin is browned and the thickest part reads 175°F (79°C).
Rest the thighs 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss 120 g mixed greens (about 5 cups) with 15 g olive oil (1 tbsp), salt, and pepper.
Serve the thighs over the dressed salad.
Finish the meal with 170 g nonfat Greek yogurt (3/4 cup) topped with 80 g blueberries (1/2 cup).

name: Sunday Steak and Roast Veg
description: Lowest-carb day dinner: steak with a big roasted vegetable plate. High protein · Low carb · ~679 kcal, 74g protein, 20g carbs, 7g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut 150 g broccoli into florets, slice 120 g zucchini (1 medium) into half-moons, and cut 100 g bell pepper (1 pepper) into strips.
Toss the vegetables with 14 g olive oil (1 tbsp), salt, and pepper; spread on a sheet pan and roast 20-25 minutes, flipping once, until the edges brown.
Pat 250 g sirloin steak dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Grill or sear in a hot pan 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, 130°F (54°C) (go to 140°F / 60°C for medium).
Rest the steak 5-10 minutes, then slice against the grain.
Plate the sliced steak with the roasted vegetables and pour any resting juices over the top.

name: Comeback Post-Lift Shake
description: The 7:15pm shake: whey in almond milk — nothing that slows it down. High protein · Quick · ~202 kcal, 32g protein, 10g carbs, 1g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pour 350 g unsweetened almond milk (about 1 1/2 cups) into a shaker bottle or blender.
Add 40 g whey protein powder (about 1 1/2 scoops).
Shake hard for 20-30 seconds, or blend with a handful of ice, until completely smooth with no clumps.
Drink right away, ideally within an hour of finishing your lift.

name: Turkey Chili
description: A big pot of bean-and-turkey chili — corn-free by design. High protein · High fiber · ~504 kcal, 50g protein, 35g carbs, 12g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 100 g onion (1 small) and 250 g tomatoes (2 medium).
Heat 12 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a pot over medium-high heat and soften the onion 3-4 minutes.
Add the ground turkey (450 g cooked weight — start with about 550 g raw) and brown it, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in 8 g spice blend (1 tbsp — chili powder or the catalog's curry-style mix both work) and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 300 g cooked black beans (1 3/4 cups, drained), the tomatoes, 150 g salsa (2/3 cup), and a splash of water; season with salt.
Simmer uncovered 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened; taste and adjust salt.
Divide into 3 containers.

name: Baja Cod Tacos
description: Flaky cod in flour tortillas with crunchy slaw. High protein · ~669 kcal, 51g protein, 54g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat 180 g cod dry and season with salt and pepper.
Bake the cod 12-15 minutes until it flakes easily and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Meanwhile, whisk 15 g olive oil mayo (1 tbsp) with 10 g lemon juice (2 tsp) and a pinch of salt, then toss with 80 g shredded cabbage (1 cup) to make the slaw.
Warm 90 g flour tortillas (2 medium) in a dry skillet, about 30 seconds per side.
Flake the cod into big chunks and divide between the tortillas.
Top each taco with slaw and 50 g avocado (1/3 avocado), sliced.

name: Greek Chicken Bowl
description: Chicken, rice, cucumber and feta with lemon-oil dressing. High protein · ~721 kcal, 70g protein, 49g carbs, 4g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Pat 190 g chicken breast (1 breast) dry and season with salt and pepper.
Grill or pan-sear over medium-high heat 5-6 minutes per side until it reaches 165°F (74°C); rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Warm 160 g cooked brown rice (about 3/4 cup) and spoon it into a bowl.
Dice 90 g cucumber and 80 g tomato.
Whisk 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) with 10 g lemon juice (2 tsp), salt, and pepper for the dressing.
Arrange the chicken, cucumber, and tomato over the rice, crumble 35 g feta (1/4 cup) on top, and drizzle with the dressing.

name: Shrimp Scampi Pasta
description: Garlic-butter shrimp over pasta with lemon. High protein · ~676 kcal, 61g protein, 60g carbs, 9g fiber per serving.
instructions:
If starting from dry pasta, boil about 100 g whole wheat pasta in salted water until al dente to yield 220 g cooked (about 2 cups); reserve a splash of pasta water before draining.
Melt 12 g butter (1 tbsp) with 8 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add 180 g cooked shrimp and warm 2-3 minutes until heated through — don't overcook or they turn rubbery.
Add 15 g lemon juice (1 tbsp) and a splash of the pasta water, then toss the pasta into the skillet to coat.
Off the heat, add 15 g grated parmesan (2 tbsp) and plenty of black pepper; toss until glossy and serve.

name: Bulk Breakfast Burrito
description: Eggs, sausage, cheese and potatoes in a big tortilla. Weight gain · High protein · ~973 kcal, 62g protein, 75g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 120 g baked potato (1 small) and 100 g cooked turkey sausage.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-high with cooking spray and crisp the potato 3-4 minutes; add the sausage for the last minute to warm.
Whisk 150 g eggs (3 large) with salt and pepper, pour into the pan, and scramble until just set.
Warm the 90 g flour tortilla (1 large) in a dry skillet, about 30 seconds per side, so it rolls without cracking.
Pile the eggs, potato, and sausage down the center, top with 40 g cheddar (1/3 cup shredded) so it melts, and spoon on 40 g salsa (2-3 tbsp).
Fold in the sides and roll tight; sear seam-side down 1 minute to seal if you like.

name: Salmon Avocado Toast
description: Smoked salmon and avocado on whole wheat. High protein · Quick · ~432 kcal, 28g protein, 40g carbs, 10g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Toast 80 g whole wheat bread (2 slices) until golden.
Mash 80 g avocado (about half a large avocado) with 5 g lemon juice (1 tsp), salt, and pepper.
Spread the mash evenly over both slices.
Layer 90 g smoked salmon on top and finish with a crack of black pepper.

name: Pork Loin with Roasted Apples
description: Sweet-savory pork with apples and green beans. High protein · ~511 kcal, 60g protein, 31g carbs, 8g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat 220 g pork tenderloin dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Core 150 g apple (1 medium) and cut it into wedges.
Set the pork on a sheet pan with the apple wedges around it and roast 20-25 minutes until the pork reaches 145°F (63°C) at the center.
Rest the pork 5-10 minutes, then slice into medallions.
While the pork rests, trim 150 g green beans (2 cups) and steam or boil 4-5 minutes until crisp-tender; toss with 10 g butter (2 tsp) and salt.
Plate the sliced pork with the roasted apples and buttered green beans.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice, chicken and egg — better than takeout. High protein · ~785 kcal, 62g protein, 77g carbs, 3g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Dice 150 g grilled chicken breast and cut 60 g carrots (1 small) into small dice.
Heat 12 g olive oil (1 tbsp) in a wide skillet or wok over high heat and stir-fry the carrots 2 minutes.
Add 250 g cooked white rice (1 1/4 cups — cold, day-old rice fries best), press it flat, and let it sizzle 2 minutes before tossing.
Push the rice to one side, crack in 50 g egg (1 large), scramble it in the open space, then fold it through the rice.
Add the chicken and 20 g soy sauce (generous 1 tbsp); toss 1-2 minutes until everything is hot and the rice picks up color.

name: PB Banana Gainer Sandwich
description: The calorie sandwich: peanut butter, banana, honey. Weight gain · Vegetarian · Quick · ~622 kcal, 24g protein, 81g carbs, 11g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Toast 90 g whole wheat bread (2 thick slices) if you like it warm; otherwise use it straight.
Spread 45 g peanut butter (3 tbsp) across both slices.
Slice 100 g banana (1 small) into coins and shingle them over one slice.
Drizzle 15 g honey (2 tsp) over the banana, close the sandwich, press gently, and cut in half.

name: Chicken Vegetable Soup
description: The rebuild-day soup: chicken and six vegetables. High protein · Low carb · Weight loss · ~364 kcal, 50g protein, 15g carbs, 5g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 120 g carrots (2 medium) into coins, chop 100 g celery (3 stalks) and 80 g onion, slice 120 g zucchini (1 medium) into half-moons, and strip and chop 80 g kale (2 cups).
Heat 10 g olive oil (2 tsp) in a soup pot over medium heat and sweat the onion, carrots, and celery 5 minutes until softening.
Add about 4 cups (1 L) water with a good pinch of salt and pepper and bring to a simmer.
Cube 300 g grilled chicken breast and add it with the zucchini; simmer gently 20 minutes until the carrots are tender.
Stir in the kale for the last 5 minutes until it wilts and softens; taste and adjust the seasoning.
Divide into 2 bowls or containers.

name: Cauliflower Shepherd's Pie
description: Beef and vegetables under whipped cauliflower. High protein · Low carb · ~520 kcal, 50g protein, 19g carbs, 6g fiber per serving.
instructions:
Cut 400 g cauliflower (1 small head) into florets and boil or steam 10-12 minutes until very tender.
Drain well and mash with 15 g butter (1 tbsp), salt, and pepper until smooth.
Meanwhile, dice 80 g onion and 100 g carrots; saute in a skillet with cooking spray over medium heat 4-5 minutes until softening.
Add the lean ground beef (350 g cooked weight — start with about 430 g raw), brown it while breaking it up, then season with salt and pepper and simmer with a splash of water 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Spread the beef mixture in a small baking dish and top with the cauliflower mash, roughing the surface with a fork.
Bake 20 minutes until the peaks of the mash brown at the edges.
Cool slightly and divide into 2 portions.
